chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from Muhammad ibn Uthman, he said: Narrated to us Ahmad, he said: Narrated to us Ubaidullah ibn Umar, he said: Narrated to us Sulayman ibn Ahmar, he said: Narrated to us Ibn Aun, from Al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samra, who said:

It was mentioned that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people of this religion will continue to be victorious over those who oppose them until there are twelve Caliphs.' So the people were standing and sitting, and he spoke a word that I did not understand, so I asked my father—or my brother: 'What did he say?' He replied: 'They are all from Quraish.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of Caliphs and their tribe?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, this narration from Jabir ibn Samra confirms the twelve Caliphs' Quraishi lineage, a detail that Shia scholars use to reconcile Sunni reports with the specific Imamate of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a foundational proof for the fixed number of Imams, linking the continuity of divine guidance to the tribal prestige of the Prophet’s family.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 93 - It is narrated from the same chains of narrators from Muhammad bin Uthman that: Narrated to us Ahmad that: Narrated to us Ubaidullah bin Uthman that: Narrated to us Sulaiman bin Ahmar that: Narrated to us Ibn Aun from Shobi from Jabir bin Samra that:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: The people of this religion would be helped [through the Caliph of God] against those who intend harm to them and this help would continue till the tenure of the twelve Caliphs. Since people were going and coming, I could not make out what the Prophet said after that. So I asked my father or brother: What did the Prophet say? He replied: All the twelve Caliphs would be from Quraish.
